sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Well, there you go, Roger.
sentences.zh: 好吧，就是这样，罗杰。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, there's a couple ways to kind of, I mean, guess at what Roger is saying here.
sentences.zh: 所以，关于罗杰在这里所说的情况，大致可以从几个角度来理解。

sentences.en: But, I mean, first is we all are very, very busy.
sentences.zh: 不过，我的意思是，首先我们大家都很忙，非常忙。

sentences.en: And, you know, often that's kind of the joke, right?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，这通常算是个笑话吧？

sentences.en: It's a good thing.
sentences.zh: 这是件好事。

sentences.en: If you weren't busy, you should be scared, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你不忙，你该害怕了，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 对，完全如此。

sentences.en: You might not be working at that place for much longer.
sentences.zh: 你可能在那家公司干不了多久了。

sentences.en: So, being busy is, like, very, like, normal.
sentences.zh: 所以，忙碌是非常，非常正常的。

sentences.en: It's good.
sentences.zh: 这很好。

sentences.en: And then, also, I mean, we work in a world where people don't necessarily understand programming.
sentences.zh: 而且，话说回来，我们身处这样一个世界：人们并不一定真正理解编程。

sentences.en: So, many of us work for people who aren't engineers or technical or programmers.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们当中许多人为那些并非工程师、不懂技术或不是程序员的人工作。

sentences.en: We have a very hard time understanding that kind of workflow that we have.
sentences.zh: 他们很难理解我们那种工作流程。

sentences.en: And then, even if you do work for those people, engineering, software engineering is still relatively new.
sentences.zh: 再者，即使你为懂技术的人工作，工程学、软件工程仍然是一门相对较新的学科。

sentences.en: So, this whole idea of estimating how much stuff should take and how many people to put on something, we're just still not really that good at.
sentences.zh: 所以，对于评估一项任务需要花多少时间、该安排多少人去做这种事，我们其实都还不是很擅长。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 对，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And so, everything is so new and different.
sentences.zh: 因此，一切都那么新颖多变。

sentences.en: And you don't know what obstacles you're going to run into.
sentences.zh: 你根本不知道会遇到什么阻碍。

sentences.en: So, often, you find yourself overloaded at work.
sentences.zh: 所以，你经常会发现自己在工作中不堪重负。

sentences.en: I mean, this is very common.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这非常普遍。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And, I mean, a lot of people, you know, feel like, oh, I'm coding in, like, assembly for this Motorola chip to power a traffic light or something like that.
sentences.zh: 而且，我的意思是，很多人，你知道的，会觉得，哦，我是在为摩托罗拉芯片编写汇编代码来驱动红绿灯之类的东西。

sentences.en: It's like, I should be working on, like, doing stuff in the web using some crazy high-level language and all these things.
sentences.zh: 他们会想，我本应该在做网络相关的东西，使用一些疯狂的高级语言和各种新技术。

sentences.en: And big data, I'm hearing that's the latest thing and all that.
sentences.zh: 还有大数据，我听说这是最新的东西，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And so, you know, I think that there is something to be said for sort of just really diving deep into technology.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我觉得有一点说得对，那就是真正深入钻研技术。

sentences.en: Even if that technology isn't the latest, greatest thing, you could still have a lot of experience just on, you know, something that you're working on now.
sentences.zh: 即使这项技术不是最新、最酷的东西，你光凭目前正在从事的工作也能积累大量经验。

sentences.en: And there's still a lot of value there, right?
sentences.zh: 这里面仍然蕴含着巨大的价值，对吧？

sentences.en: So, you shouldn't worry so much about, oh, I'm not doing the latest thing, right, that I'm reading about in the news.
sentences.zh: 所以，你不必过分担心，哦，我没有在做那些我在新闻里读到的最新技术，对吧？

sentences.en: Because the latest thing will get old.
sentences.zh: 因为最新的技术终究会过时。

sentences.en: Either the latest thing will get old or it will die, right?
sentences.zh: 要么最新的技术变旧，要么它消亡，对吧？

sentences.en: Either of those two are very good.
sentences.zh: 这两者中的任何一个都非常正常。

sentences.en: So, you know, in general, those deep, those deep, those deep, those deep, Jason.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，总的来说，那些深厚的，那些深厚的，那些深厚的，那些深厚的，杰森。

sentences.en: But, yeah, I mean, I think that his point, which is very salient, too, is just to continue to do side projects and keep yourself up to date.
sentences.zh: 不过，对，我的意思是，我觉得他的观点也非常切中要害，那就是继续做业余项目来保持自我更新。

sentences.en: But it's hard to find time with that.
sentences.zh: 但要抽出时间很难。

sentences.en: You have life, you have work.
sentences.zh: 你要生活，你要工作。

sentences.en: So, you can be overwhelmed at work like I was discussing, you know, and just feel bad and then not have time for the other stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会像我刚才讨论的那样，在工作中被压得喘不过气来，然后感到沮丧，接着就没有时间去搞别的东西了。

sentences.en: Or even the other way, Jason's interpretation of this, like, feeling behind and that you're not working on the latest and greateSt.
sentences.zh: 或者反过来，按照杰森对这句话的解读，就像是感觉落后了，觉得自己在从事的不是最新、最棒的工作。

sentences.en: But, I mean, for the most part, that's always going to be the case.
sentences.zh: 但是，我的意思是，在大多数情况下，情况一直都会是这样的。

sentences.en: Some companies kind of pick a thing and stick with it.
sentences.zh: 有些公司会选定某项技术然后坚持使用。

sentences.en: And so, you're, even if you worked on that cutting edge company, working on that cutting edge thing, likely in two, three, four, five years, that thing is now the mature,
sentences.zh: 所以，哪怕你在那种走在前沿的公司工作，做着前沿的技术，很可能在两、三、四、五年后，那项技术就会变成成熟、

sentences.en: safe project that everybody's using, right?
sentences.zh: 安全的项目，所有人都在使用，对吧？

sentences.en: And you would have to, like, this would be a dangerous thing if you always had to work on the cutting edge thing.
sentences.zh: 如果你必须永远追逐前沿技术，那将是一件非常危险的事情。

sentences.en: So, I do think it is important to have some level of side projects or reading or watching YouTube videos or trying to just learn new language.
sentences.zh: 因此，我确实认为，保持一定程度的业余项目开发、阅读、观看 YouTube 视频或尝试学习新语言是很重要的。

sentences.en: I mean, whatever it is, you know, to try to stimulate that, you know, keep your brain working and learning.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不管是什么，你知道的，尽量去刺激一下，你知道的，让你的大脑保持运转和学习。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, like, right now, at least from what I've been reading, Ruby on Rails is kind of, like, the big buzzword, you know?
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，就像现在，至少从我读到的内容来看，Ruby on Rails 某种程度上就像是一个热门流行语，你知道吗？

sentences.en: It's, like, the hot thing.
sentences.zh: 它就像是最热门的东西。

sentences.en: Dude, I think that was, like, years ago.
sentences.zh: 老兄，我觉得那已经是好几年前的事了。

sentences.en: Well, what's the hot thing now?
sentences.zh: 好吧，那现在什么东西最火？

sentences.en: I think, like, I mean, it even passes, like, to Node.js, and then now even that's a year or two old, so it's even past that.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，我的意思是，它甚至超越了 Node.js，而现在 Node.js 也已经过了一两年了，所以它甚至超越了那个。

sentences.en: Oh, man, I'm falling behind.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我落伍了。

sentences.en: I think, I think, actually, my side projects.
sentences.zh: 我想，我想实际上，我的业余项目……

sentences.en: I mean, it's not exactly the same, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，情况不完全一样，对吧？

sentences.en: But, I mean, like, the buzzwords keep, like, I mean, it's always going to be something new.
sentences.zh: 但是，我的意思是，那些流行语不断出现，我的意思是，总会有新东西出来的。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: He doesn't know what they are.
sentences.zh: 他根本不知道那些是什么。

sentences.en: I have no idea how to do them.
sentences.zh: 我完全不知道怎么做它们。

sentences.en: But, yeah, I mean, you know, knowing about the latest and greatest thing is good, and having that breadth is good, but it's not something to really worry about.
sentences.zh: 不过，对，我的意思是，你知道的，了解最新、最棒的技术是好事，拥有这种知识广度也是好事，但它并不是一件需要真正去担忧的事。

sentences.en: And like Patrick said, there's...
sentences.zh: 就像帕特里克说的，还有……

sentences.en: So, but what if he's still programming in COBOL?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果他还在用 COBOL 编程呢？

sentences.en: If he's still programming in COBOL?
sentences.zh: 如果他还在用 COBOL 编程？

sentences.en: Well, he's good he's watching the show or listening to the show.
sentences.zh: 那他挺庆幸自己正在看这个节目或者听这个节目。

sentences.en: So, but, I mean, there's a limit to it, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，但是，我的意思是，这是有局限性的，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, so, if the language, with anything, you know, we don't know the situation.
sentences.zh: 比如说，如果这门语言，对于任何事情，你知道的，我们不了解具体情况。

sentences.en: You're just going to do the best you can.
sentences.zh: 你只能尽力而为。

sentences.en: We feel you.
sentences.zh: 我们感同身受。

sentences.en: We understand the pain you're in.
sentences.zh: 我们理解你所经历的痛苦。

sentences.en: But, I mean, you've got to kind of...
sentences.zh: 但是，我的意思是，你必须某种程度上……

sentences.en: If you're using a language that...
sentences.zh: 如果你使用的语言……

sentences.en: Nothing wrong with COBOL.
sentences.zh: COBOL 没什么毛病。

sentences.en: There's, you know, lots of good money, I'm sure, to be made working jobs where you're programming COBOL.
sentences.zh: 你懂的，通过编写 COBOL 的工作，肯定能赚到很多不错的薪水。

sentences.en: But there's a balance of, like, you know, understanding what risks and things you're taking on.
sentences.zh: 但这里存在一个平衡，比如，你知道的，要明白你在承担什么样的风险。

sentences.en: And if you're working in a language or environment that is still being used by newer stuff, then you're probably pretty much okay.
sentences.zh: 如果你使用的语言或环境仍在被更新的技术所使用，那你大概就没什么大碍。

sentences.en: So, you think of, like, Java, C++, even C, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，你想想，比如 Java、C++，甚至 C，对吧？

sentences.en: These things are still being used actively today.
sentences.zh: 这些东西今天仍然在被积极使用。

sentences.en: So, that's still a fertile field.
sentences.zh: 所以这仍然是一片肥沃的土地。

sentences.en: Then you shouldn't be too scared.
sentences.zh: 那你就不应该太害怕。

sentences.en: But if you are on something that basically it's all maintenance all the time, that's dangerous because if you know and that's, like, your thing and you're going to embrace it,
sentences.zh: 但如果你从事的是那种基本上全部都是维护工作的领域，那就很危险了，因为如果你清楚这一点并且，这就好比是你的菜，你决定全盘接受，

sentences.en: great.
sentences.zh: 那也挺好。

sentences.en: But otherwise, those number of projects still on that are going to get smaller and smaller to some level.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，这类依然存在的项目数量在某种程度上会越来越少。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And so, that's risky.
sentences.zh: 所以，这很有风险。

sentences.en: And then, also, you don't learn that how to kind of code brand new things because you're just stuck in maintenance all the time.
sentences.zh: 而且，你也不会学到如何编写全新的东西，因为你总是被困在维护工作中。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And to Patrick's point, just to say it a different way, it really depends on what you're working on much more than the language, right?
sentences.zh: 顺着帕特里克的观点，换一种说法，这真的取决于你在做什么，而不是取决于语言，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, you could be doing...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可能在做……

sentences.en: So, I do a lot of C++, and C++ isn't, like, the newest, sexiest language.
sentences.zh: 所以，我做很多 C++，而 C++ 并不是那种最新、最性感的语言。

sentences.en: But I feel like I'm working on something that is pretty new and interesting, right?
sentences.zh: 但我感觉我正在做的事情相当新颖而且有趣，对吧？

sentences.en: And so, that's really the thing you should look for.
sentences.zh: 所以这才是你真正应该寻找的东西。

sentences.zh: 等等，但刚刚不是出了 C++ 0X 吗，对吧？

sentences.en: It just, like...
sentences.zh: 它刚刚，就像……

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，对。

sentences.en: It's new, right?
sentences.zh: 它是新的，对吧？

sentences.zh: 对，我们还没升级到那个版本。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧。

sentences.en: Actually, I take it back.
sentences.zh: 其实，我收回刚才的话。

sentences.en: I think C++ OX is supported, but I don't know it yet.
sentences.zh: 我觉得 C++ 0X 已经受支持了，但我还不会用它。

sentences.en: So, I know, like, I know a few things, but nothing too big.
sentences.zh: 所以，我了解，比如，我知道一些皮毛，但没什么大不了的。

sentences.en: But, yeah.
sentences.zh: 不过，对。

sentences.en: So, but, you know, to Patrick's point, if you're happy with your job and you're doing some fun, interesting things, that's really what matters.
sentences.zh: 所以，不过，你知道的，就帕трик（Patrick）的观点来看，如果你对自己的工作感到满意，并且在做一些有趣、好玩的事情，那才是真正重要的。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's good that you're doing the side projects so that if the job does get stale for you, you can go and you'll have the latest tech under your belt.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，你在做一些副业是很好的，这样如果工作对你来说变得枯燥乏味了，你就可以去尝试，并且还能掌握最新的技术。

sentences.zh: 它拥有极快的哈希表，还能让你使用lambda表达式，以及各种超级有趣的功能。

sentences.en: But it's also very niche, right?
sentences.zh: 但它也很小众，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, there are things that you don't want to write in Lisp.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有些东西你是不想用Lisp来写的。

sentences.en: You don't want to write, you know, like a file I.O.
sentences.zh: 你不会想要用Lisp去编写，

sentences.en: library in Lisp.
sentences.zh: 比如一个文件I/O库。

sentences.en: It's like painful, right?
sentences.zh: 那太痛苦了，对吧？

sentences.en: So, you know, you can actually integrate, you can go seamlessly between Java and any of these languages.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，你实际上可以进行集成，你可以在Java和所有这些语言之间无缝切换。

sentences.en: So you can take the part of your problem that you're trying to solve, that's very easily solved by Lisp, and you can do that part in Lisp and then do the rest of your program
sentences.zh: 所以你可以把你要解决的问题中可以由Lisp轻松解决的那部分，用Lisp来做，然后把程序的其余部分

sentences.en: in Java and they'll just communicate with each other and it'll work.
sentences.zh: 用Java来做，它们会互相通信，并且能够正常工作。

sentences.en: It'll work very fluidly.
sentences.zh: 它会非常流畅地运行。

sentences.en: The other thing is I think Clojure also adds some pretty advanced stuff.
sentences.zh: 另一件事是，我认为Clojure还添加了一些相当高级的东西。

sentences.en: I think they add like a software transactional memory.
sentences.zh: 我想他们添加了类似软件事务内存（STM）的东西。

sentences.en: Which maybe we'll talk about one episode.
sentences.zh: 也许我们在某一集里会谈到它。

sentences.en: So they do add some things and Lisp has all these dialects, I guess, are kind of what they're called.
sentences.zh: 所以他们确实添加了一些东西，而且Lisp有所有这些方言，我猜这大概就是它们的称呼。

sentences.en: But Lisp has all these dialects and Clojure, I don't know, consider one of them or not, but it does add its own set of flavor to what it kind of does better or different than the
sentences.zh: 但是Lisp有所有这些方言，而Clojure，我不知道，算不算其中之一，但它确实为现有的Lisp增添了它自己的一套特色，使其在做得更好或与众不同方面别具一格

sentences.en: existing Lisp in addition to all of the JVM advantages you get and having the macros set up where you're able to call Java APIs, you know, from your Clojure code.
sentences.zh: 除了你获得的JVM的所有优势，以及设置了宏使你能够从Clojure代码中调用Java API之外，它还有这些特点。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 对，对，完全如此。

sentences.en: I mean, I did a lot of Lisp programming in college and I never did anything with a GUI.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我在大学里写过很多Lisp程序，但我从没用它做过任何带GUI的东西。

sentences.en: Like there are times I wanted a GUI, but I just, you know, with Lisp, it's like if there
sentences.zh: 就像有时我想要一个GUI，但我只是，你知道的，对于Lisp来说，如果有什么方法的话

sentences.en: was some way, it'd probably be some Lisp GTK, like crazy hackery that probably wouldn't work half the time, right?
sentences.zh: 那大概会是什么Lisp GTK之类的疯狂黑客手段，可能有一半时间都无法工作，对吧？

sentences.en: And it's just, it's just kind of, that stuff's super ugly, right?
sentences.zh: 而且那，那感觉超级丑陋，对吧？

sentences.en: But, you know, the JVM has sort of taken a lot of that complexity away.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，JVM在某种程度上带走了许多这样的复杂性。

sentences.en: Okay, so you could write, you know, a Clojure program that has like a GUI built into it and lets you like, you know, visualize results in a way that's more appealing, you know, and
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以你可以编写，你知道的，一个带有内置GUI的Clojure程序，让你可以，你知道的，以一种更吸引人的方式可视化结果，你知道的

sentences.en: you'd have much higher productivity than if you're writing in straight lists.
sentences.zh: 而且你的生产力会比直接用纯Lisp编写高得多。

sentences.en: And I guess, I mean, I remembered a point during this discussion about that running on the JVM also brings us security.
sentences.zh: 我想，我在这次讨论中还记起的一点是，在JVM上运行也给我们带来了安全性。

sentences.en: So when you run a C++ application, you don't know what that, you're basically letting that,
sentences.zh: 所以当你运行一个C++应用程序时，你并不知道那个，你基本上是在让那个东西——

sentences.en: aside from what the OS provides, you're letting that thing do whatever you want, whatever it wants to.
sentences.zh: 除了操作系统提供的内容之外，你是在让它做任何你想做的事，任何它想做的事。

sentences.en: But the JVM, barring recent exploits that were discovered, I mean, the JVM has this notion of security.
sentences.zh: 但JVM，除了最近发现的一些漏洞之外，我的意思是，JVM有这种安全概念。

sentences.en: So you're supposed to be able to run untrusted code.
sentences.zh: 所以你应该能够运行不受信任的代码。

sentences.en: And if you don't want to let that code access the file system, it's not supposed to be able to break out of that virtual machine.
sentences.zh: 如果你不想让该代码访问文件系统，它就不应该能够突破那个虚拟机的限制。

sentences.en: So it's not supposed to be able to do stuff you don't want it to do.
sentences.zh: 所以它不应该去做那些你不想让它做的事情。

sentences.en: And so when you run Clojure, for instance, in the JVM, you're getting that added ability to kind of have that feeling of security.
sentences.zh: 因此，当你例如在 JVM 中运行 Clojure 时，你会获得那种额外的能力，从而带来那种安全感。

sentences.en: I mean, there are whole teams from many different, like, you know, multi-corporate, you know, consortia that are looking into JVM security.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有许多不同团队，比如你知道的，来自多个公司的企业联合体，都在研究 JVM 安全性。

sentences.en: There's probably next to nobody looking into LISP, you know, the C-LISP security, right?
sentences.zh: 大概几乎没有人去研究 LISP，你知道的，C-LISP 的安全性，对吧？

sentences.en: So, yeah, you get the benefit of all these resources.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，你可以享受到所有这些资源带来的好处。

sentences.en: So our final language is Scala.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的最后一种语言是 Scala。

sentences.en: Scala takes a little bit of a different bent than these in that it doesn't port an existing language to the JVM or an existing language concept to the JVM.
sentences.zh: Scala 与这些语言略有不同，因为它并不是将现有的语言移植到 JVM 上，也不是将现有的语言概念移植到 JVM 上。

sentences.en: It instead tries to be kind of everything Java is, but even better.
sentences.zh: 相反，它试图成为 Java 能做的一切，甚至还要更好。

sentences.en: So it tries to be its own thing.
sentences.zh: 所以它试图走自己的路。

sentences.en: And so some of the interesting things about Scala is that it's both functional and object-oriented.
sentences.zh: Scala 比较有趣的一个特点是，它既是函数式的，又是面向对象的。

sentences.en: So you can kind of, like, pick both of whatever you need from the strengths of both of those in your code.
sentences.zh: 所以你在代码中可以同时汲取这两者的优势，按需选用。

sentences.en: It gets all these benefits we've already talked about, about really good compatibility
sentences.zh: 它继承了我们之前讨论过的所有优势，比如拥有非常好的兼容性

sentences.en: with the existing JVM.
sentences.zh: 与现有的 JVM。

sentences.en: And the nice thing about Scala being a new language and kind of trying to extend upon the Java syntax is sometimes writing Scala code, you know, I'm doing air quotes here, is as
sentences.zh: Scala 作为一门新语言的好处在于，它试图对 Java 语法进行扩展，有时候编写 Scala 代码——你知道，我这里在打引号——其实

sentences.en: simple as just, like, making a very few modifications to existing Java code.
sentences.zh: 很简单，只需对现有的 Java 代码做一点点修改即可。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: And then once you do that, you may be able to do some concept that would have taken you many, many, many lines of Java code and it's just a few lines of Scala code.
sentences.zh: 然后一旦你这样做了，你可能就能实现某些概念，如果用 Java 代码写需要好长好长好长的篇幅，而用 Scala 只需要几行代码。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, anyone who's done, you know, raw Java on Android has been through the pain of runnables.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，任何在 Android 上写过原生 Java 的人，都经历过 Runnable（可运行对象）的痛苦。

sentences.en: So Java has this thing called runnable and the idea is, you know, this is something that you want to run in another thread.
sentences.zh: 所以 Java 有个叫 Runnable 的东西，其核心思想是，你知道的，这是你想要在另一个线程中运行的东西。

sentences.en: So a runnable, you know, on the surface a runnable just has, is just a class with a run function.
sentences.zh: 所以 Runnable，表面上看，Runnable 只有、也就是一个带有 run 函数的类。

sentences.en: So there's not much to that.
sentences.zh: 所以它没多少复杂的内容。

sentences.en: But the idea is many of these thread, like a thread pool in Java or, you know, a single thread, if you want to kick off a thread, we'll use, we'll take a runnable as a parameter
sentences.zh: 但这个想法是，许多这样的线程，比如 Java 中的线程池，或者，你知道的，单个线程，如果你想启动一个线程，我们会使用、会将一个 Runnable 作为参数

sentences.en: and then execute the run function in another thread.
sentences.zh: 然后在另一个线程中执行 run 函数。

sentences.en: But the thing about Android is Android doesn't want you to lock the OS, right?
sentences.zh: 但 Android 的问题在于，Android 不希望你卡住操作系统，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, they don't want you to do something that paralyzes the person's phone.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们不希望你做一些会让用户的手机瘫痪的事情。

sentences.en: And so they really encourage you to do everything in other threads.
sentences.zh: 所以他们极力鼓励你在其他线程中完成所有事情。

sentences.en: And what this means is you have just tons of these like runnable, these like container classes that don't have any data in them.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你会有大量这样的 Runnable，就像那种里面没有任何数据的容器类。

sentences.en: They're just classes so that you can call a run function.
sentences.zh: 它们只是类，这样你就可以调用一个 run 函数。

sentences.en: And your code kind of gets kind of ugly.
sentences.zh: 然后你的代码就会变得有点丑陋。

sentences.en: It's very hard to write clean code this way.
sentences.zh: 用这种方式很难写出整洁的代码。

sentences.en: Well, Scala, because it has the option of being functional, sort of gets around this.
sentences.zh: 好吧，Scala 因为可以选择函数式编程，所以某种程度上绕过了这个问题。

sentences.en: I mean, functions become objects and you can just pass them around to different methods.
sentences.zh: 我是说，函数变成了对象，你可以把它们随手传递给不同的方法。

sentences.en: So you could pass a function to a, you know, around to the Android OS and it'll run it.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以把一个函数传递给，你知道的，传给 Android 操作系统，它就会运行它。

sentences.en: And it just makes the code look cleaner.
sentences.zh: 这让代码看起来更清爽。

sentences.en: So Scala is being used.
sentences.zh: 所以 Scala 正在被广泛使用。

sentences.en: The other thing about what functional programming gets you is a lot of, it lends itself to distributed
sentences.zh: 函数式编程带来的另一个好处是，在许多人看来，它比面向对象编程

sentences.en: processing more readily in many people's opinion than, you know, object-oriented programming, for instance.
sentences.zh: 更能自然地适应分布式处理。

sentences.en: And so you'll see there are a number of, well, for several of these, but for Scala in particular, a number of very highly distributed web apps that use it.
sentences.zh: 所以你会发现有相当一部分——虽然有些语言也有，但特别是 Scala，有很多高度分布式的高流量 Web 应用都在使用它。

sentences.en: So Twitter has come out and said that they use Scala and they've actually been big contributors.
sentences.zh: 所以 Twitter 已经公开表示他们在使用 Scala，而且他们实际上一直是重要的贡献者。

sentences.en: They released a set of learning guides for Scala if you're interested.
sentences.zh: 如果你感兴趣的话，他们发布了一套 Scala 的学习指南。

sentences.en: So that's actually what they use for their new engineers.
sentences.zh: 所以这实际上就是他们为新工程师准备的培训内容。

sentences.en: People who are experienced software engineers but new to Scala, that's what they use to teach them.
sentences.zh: 对于经验丰富的软件工程师但对 Scala 还不熟悉的人，他们就是用这个来教他们的。

sentences.en: So that's a recommended source of learning.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个推荐的学习来源。

sentences.en: Foursquare is known to use specifically one of the web frameworks of Scala, the Lyft framework.
sentences.zh: Foursquare 众所周知专门使用了 Scala 的一个 Web 框架，即 Lyft 框架。

sentences.en: And so I'm pretty sure they'll probably help out contributing to that as well.
sentences.zh: 所以我很确凿他们可能也会对该框架的贡献提供帮助。

sentences.en: But that's something they've come out and said that they use.
sentences.zh: 但这是他们公开承认过自己在使用的技术。

sentences.en: And those are something that there are web frameworks for other languages and stuff.
sentences.zh: 虽然其他语言也有相应的 Web 框架之类的东西。

sentences.en: But many of these JVM-based languages do seem to have a strong web framework presence or really good web frameworks that seem really well supported.
sentences.zh: 但许多基于 JVM 的语言似乎确实在 Web 框架方面有着很强的存在感，或者说拥有非常优秀且似乎支持力度很大的 Web 框架。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, one thing Java got extremely well was the whole web movement.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，Java 把握得极好的一点就是整个 Web 浪潮。

sentences.en: Like, Java was essential to that.
sentences.zh: 比如，Java 对此至关重要。

sentences.en: I mean, they started JSP.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们开启了 JSP。

sentences.en: They had Tomcat, which is a fantastic web server container.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有 Tomcat，这是一个出色的 Web 服务器容器。

sentences.en: And so anytime you can hook into Java, you can take advantage of all of this history.
sentences.zh: 所以只要你能接入 Java，你就能利用所有这些历史积累。

sentences.en: The other thing, in the last episode, we talked about Hadoop and HBase and all of these libraries associated with big data.
sentences.zh: 另一件事是，在上期节目中，我们讨论了 Hadoop、HBase 以及所有与大数据相关的库。

sentences.en: All of that is written in Java.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都是用 Java 编写的。

sentences.en: But if you're using one of these languages, you naturally can hook into those.
sentences.zh: 但如果你在使用这些语言之一，你自然就能与它们对接。

sentences.en: Oh, interesting.
sentences.zh: 哦，有意思。

sentences.en: So you could write a Hadoop job that runs on 10,000 machines in Python or in Lisp or in Scala.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以用 Python、Lisp 或 Scala 编写一个运行在 10,000 台机器上的 Hadoop 作业。

sentences.en: Nice.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: I think that wraps it up for this show.
sentences.zh: 我想这期节目就到这里。

sentences.en: I mean, three languages, which are interesting.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这三种语言都很有趣。

sentences.en: Maybe that's a little bit of cheating because we kind of handled them together.
sentences.zh: 也许这有点作弊，因为我们把它们放在一起讲了。

sentences.en: Well, it encourages people to go and watch those shows.
sentences.zh: 不过，这鼓励大家去收听那些相关的节目。

sentences.en: So if you haven't listened to the episode on Python, Lisp, or Scala is actually based on Scheme, which is probably something we'll cover in a future episode.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你还没听过关于 Python 的节目，Lisp 或 Scala 实际上是基于 Scheme 的，这可能是我们未来节目中会涉及的内容。

sentences.en: But yeah, check out those languages and check out those shows.
sentences.zh: 不过话说回来，去看看那些语言和相关的节目吧。

sentences.en: And yeah, it's good times.
sentences.zh: 而且，确实，那段时光很美好。

sentences.en: Awesome.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Well, I think that's a wrap.
sentences.zh: 好了，我想就这样结束吧。

sentences.en: Cool.
sentences.zh: 酷。

sentences.en: Have fun, everyone.
sentences.zh: 大家玩得开心。
